title: What are Types in TypeScript?
overview: Types define what kind of value a variable can store. TypeScript uses types to prevent invalid values and catch errors during development.

example.title: Type Example
example.content:
let username: string = 'Manthan';
let age: number = 25;

title: String Type
overview: The string type is used for storing text values. It allows TypeScript to ensure that only string values are assigned.

title: Number Type
overview: The number type is used for integer and decimal values in TypeScript.

example.title: Number Example
example.content:
let count: number = 10;
let price: number = 99.99;

title: Boolean Type
overview: The boolean type stores true or false values. It is commonly used for conditions and application states.

title: Array Type
overview: Arrays can be typed to define what type of values they can contain. This prevents adding incorrect data into arrays.

example.title: Array Example
example.content:
let names: string[] = ['John','Manthan'];

let numbers: number[] = [1,2,3];

title: Tuple Type
overview: A tuple is an array with a fixed number of elements where each element has a specific type.

title: Any and Unknown Types
overview: The any type disables type checking, while unknown is safer because the value must be checked before use.

example.title: Any vs Unknown
example.content:
let value: any = 10;

let data: unknown = 'Hello';

title: Topic Summary
overview: You learned TypeScript basic types including string, number, boolean, arrays, tuples, any, and unknown types.

example.title: Quick Revision
example.content:
✔ Types define allowed values.
✔ string stores text.
✔ number stores numeric values.
✔ boolean stores true/false.
✔ Arrays and tuples provide structured data.
